blocks.text: Many kings he turned into fakirs, and many fakirs he raised into leaders; Guru Nanak remained beyond worldly attachment, a sovereign among sovereigns. (36)
Those who touched Guru Nanak’s feet gained such power that sparrows could strike hawks and lambs could tear lions. (37)
Those who sat upon royal thrones and commanded great armies became as servants before the power awakened by the Guru. (38)
If a tyrant rose against them, he would quickly come to ruin. (39)
So I told Murray that such sovereignty belonged to Guru Nanak’s house, and that one who came into the Guru’s refuge was protected while oppressors were struck down. (40)
